::: {.why}
Week 47 turns the research pipeline into a scheduled system, and the design that matters is which failures are loud and which are silent, because the silent ones are the expensive ones.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Implement the daily run as an ordered set of steps, each with an explicit success condition rather than an absence of exceptions.
- Name the three failures that would not raise an exception and say how each is detected.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Write qlib/run/daily.py: ingest, validate, compute signals, construct the portfolio, generate orders, submit, and reconcile. Each step returns a status with the checks it performed, and a step that produced no data succeeds only if producing no data was expected on that date.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Enumerate the silent failures and add a check for each: stale data that is present but unchanged from yesterday, a signal that computed but is outside its historical range, and an order set that is empty because a join failed rather than because the strategy wanted no positions. Those three account for most silent production failures in this kind of system.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
qlib/run/daily.py is the production entry point: seven ordered steps, each with an explicit success condition, and three checks for the failures that do not raise exceptions.
:::
